name: rangescan
note: What the scanner records is a range image - one distance per direction, not a picture. Turn each distance into a position and you have the points. Grey is where the mirror has not been yet; near-black is a direction the pulse never came back from. It stops at the first thing it meets, so the cloud has the specimen's shadow in it - which is why a survey is several registered scan positions, and why occlusion gets planned before anybody presses a button. Keeping only that first return is also what makes this a surface method rather than a volume one.
